topics.topic: How EffectAttempt.authority must identify a FlowActivation (explicit activation identity vs inference, and what identifier fields are stored)
questions: When authority is a flow activation, what exact identifier/facts must be stored to point to that activation record, given M18 defines FlowActivation as an entity but gives no activation id field?
Is the exact FlowActivation entity identity part of run-pinned facts, or inferred later from timing/order?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A: the kernel records and later returns an explicit reference to the exact FlowActivation entity that authorized a `draft-write` send under "the flow activation under which the run started"; Behavior B: the kernel stores no explicit activation reference and infers authority later from run facts (for example pinned `flow_version_id` and record order/timing), which can resolve to a different activation record when the same version is re-activated; the owner/agent notices the difference when inspecting effect-attempt authority and audit trace provenance.
judgement.why: State 1 requires draft-write authority to be a specific flow activation but does not close how that specific activation is identified in stored facts.

topics.topic: Which operation node types are eligible for StandingGrant (including read/draft-write) and whether grants to draft-write have effect
questions: May a standing grant be created for `read` or `draft-write` operation nodes, or are grants valid only for nodes that can stop for approval (`state-transition` and `external-effect`)?
Can a standing grant be created for a `draft-write` node, and if so does it have any effect?

judgement.divergence: Behavior A: the kernel allows StandingGrant creation for any non-`destructive` operation node (including `read`/`draft-write`), so grant requests on those nodes succeed and appear active, even if runtime authority for `draft-write` still uses flow activation; Behavior B: the kernel rejects grants for `read`/`draft-write` as ineligible and allows grants only for nodes that can stop for approval (`state-transition`/`external-effect`), so the same grant request is refused; the owner notices via different grant-call outcomes and inspection state.
judgement.why: The texts exclude only `destructive` explicitly for grant creation while approval-stop/runtime-authority rules focus on other classes, leaving eligibility and practical effect for `read`/`draft-write` open.

topics.topic: Cancellation semantics for in-flight attempts/executing sandboxes and how they appear in model facts/traces
questions: At cancellation time, how are in-flight operation attempts and currently executing function sandboxes represented in model facts/traces?

topics.topic: Exact permissions/actions that allow reading implementation code bodies
questions: Under which exact product actions and permissions may an agent read implementation code bodies?

topics.topic: Run-end behavior on owner refusal when other branches are already running or ready
questions: When owner refusal occurs, what happens to other branches already running or ready to run in the same run?

topics.topic: What happens to grant identity when a revoked StandingGrant is granted again (new grant_id vs reactivation)
questions: If a grant was revoked and the owner grants the same flow-version node again, is that a new grant entity (new `grant_id`) or reactivation of the revoked one?

topics.topic: When non-token Installation field changes take effect (live vs only after restart)
questions: Do changes to installation fields other than token list (especially `manifest_revision`, `service_instances`, `service_credentials`) take effect only after restart, or can they take effect live while the process runs?

topics.topic: Whether State 1 is currently normative/binding or still provisional
questions: Is State 1 normative and binding for downstream states/code now, or still provisional so later writers may change model facts silently?
